messages:
Priya: Canary rollout for release v2-serving started in us-west-2 at 1830001111. Please monitor p95/p99, kv-cache hit rate, and any error spikes. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/canary/v2-serving :eyes:

aj: Noted. I'll watch p95 and trace sample. Tagging @mike for profiler dives.

infra-bot: [ALERT] 1830001180 - latency_p95_us-west-2 increased 32% vs baseline for route /v1/generate. See: https://alerts.internal/alert/8231 :rotating_light:

aj: Seeing it in the dashboard too — p95 jumped from ~160ms -> ~210-230ms around 1830001168. p99 also up. No error rate increase.

mike: Kicking off a sampling profiler and live flame on the canary nodes. Early look shows increased KV-cache evictions and smaller effective batch sizes. Possible kv shard hotness after model shard placement change in this deploy.

Sofia: I can pull logs + kcache metrics. Quick command for debug traces: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://us-west-2.internal/api/v1/debug/traces?canary=true&limit=50'```

aj: Pulled 30 traces. Median token latency per-request increased, and a few traces show repeated kvcache-miss loops: "kv_lookup->miss->fallback->kv_populate->miss". That suggests race with cache warmup.

Priya: Given the 32% p95 regression and no obvious user-impact errors but consistent latency hit for the canary cohort, proposal: hold the rollout, scale canary down to 10% traffic, and decide whether to rollback if p95 > +25% for 15m. Requesting approvals from release leads. @alex please weigh in.

alex: I approve holding and scaling to 10%. We should not instant rollback yet — gather traces and try a quick patch to KV warmup if feasible. If no improvement within 20m, revert.

mike: I'll push a cfg change to increase kvcache prefetch factor and restart a canary pod for testing. Patch will be quick but may need a minute to warm.

infra-bot: [ACTION] 1830001300 - updated canary weight from 50% -> 10% per policy.

aj: After lowering to 10%, observed p95 trend: 200ms -> 185ms over next 6 minutes. Still ~15% above baseline. Traces show fewer misses but some long tail persists.

mike: Prefetch change rolled to one canary pod at 1830001325. Logs show reduced kv miss loops. Hoping for stabilization.

Priya: Good. We'll watch 10 more minutes. If p95 doesn't return to within +10% of baseline, we plan rollback at 1830001500. Anyone object?

Sofia: Quick note for postmortem — capture shard-lookup latencies and model placement logs. I'll start a collection job now.

aj: At 1830001440 p95 still ~180ms (~12% over baseline). Trending down but not fully recovered. Given trend and patch, recommend holding but not rolling back immediately. Risk: rollback disrupts user traffic twice.

alex: Agreed with aj. Hold and continue monitoring. If trend flattens or improves by 1830001600, we can progress rollout. Otherwise we revert.

Priya: OK — holding. I'll write a short incident note and schedule a 30m sync to decide next steps. Thanks all for fast responses.

infra-bot: [LOG] 1830001450 - canary status: HOLD at 10% traffic. Metrics collection: enabled.
